commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization (#24969)

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing layouts during global optimization makes that phase target
aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding tensor
graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their epilogues and
result unpacks.

Add `--iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling`. For a module with a
single target that supports host encoding materialization
(`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported`: llvm-cpu on x86_64 or AArch64
with the CPU encoding resolver and without inner-tiled layouts), and
with the default encoding strategy, the new pass:

1. normalizes contraction dimensions,
2. assigns and propagates encodings,
3. materializes them on the host,
4. records the target (#24968).

Other modules, and the padding encoding strategy, keep dispatch-time
data tiling. The route takes its operation families and encoding
strategy from the dispatch-creation data-tiling flags, passed down from
`Pipelines.cpp`, because unsupported modules fall back to that route.

**Behavior changes that are easy to miss.**
- The flag takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags,
so conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set.
- The target is recorded even when nothing was data-tiled, so
dispatch-time assignment stays off for that module.
- The early pipeline also runs `BubbleUpExpandShapes` and `SinkReshapes`
on eligible modules.
- For modules with the attribute, dispatch creation always enables
`fuse-mmt4d` and `fuse-data-tiled-convolution` (#24967), even if they
are set to false, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions.

**Relation to existing paths.** `--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` with
early materialization also materializes on the host, but it has no
contraction normalization or propagation, and its mmt4d ops are not
fused with their epilogues. Like that path, this one relies on
`MaterializeHostEncodingPass` and is restricted to single-target
modules. The layout decision is split between this pass,
`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported` and the dispatch-creation
passes that read the attribute, and it adds HAL and Codegen dependencies
to the global phases. TODOs (#25031) describe moving it into its own
component that decides per affinity.

**Performance** on an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32,
`--iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host`, median of 10). HAL dispatches in
parentheses. x86_64 has not been measured.

| workload | dispatch-time data tiling | this PR |
`--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` |
|---|---|---|---|
| matmul 512x1024x1024 + bias + ReLU | 1.49 ms (4) | 1.50 ms (3) | 1.43
ms (4) |
| batch_matmul 16x256x512x256 + ReLU | 1.69 ms (3) | 1.68 ms (3) | 1.75
ms (4) |
| conv NHWC 1x58x58x64, 3x3x64x64 + ReLU | 10.5 ms (3) | 10.5 ms (3) |
5.68 ms (1)* |

On these workloads the new path is within noise of dispatch-time data
tiling, which already fuses epilogues inside encoded dispatches. *The
global-opt row does not data-tile the convolution, because
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` only affects
dispatch creation. On this machine the existing experimental convolution
data tiling is slower than direct convolution codegen, independent of
this PR.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

fused with their epilogues. Like that path, this one relies on
`MaterializeHostEncodingPass` and is restricted to single-target
modules. The layout decision is split between this pass,
`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported` and the dispatch-creation
passes that read the attribute, and it adds HAL and Codegen dependencies
to the global phases. TODOs (#25031) describe moving it into its own
component that decides per affinity.

**Performance** on an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32,
`--iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host`, median of 10). HAL dispatches in
parentheses. x86_64 has not been measured.

| workload | dispatch-time data tiling | this PR |
`--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` |
|---|---|---|---|
| matmul 512x1024x1024 + bias + ReLU | 1.49 ms (4) | 1.50 ms (3) | 1.43
ms (4) |
| batch_matmul 16x256x512x256 + ReLU | 1.69 ms (3) | 1.68 ms (3) | 1.75
ms (4) |
| conv NHWC 1x58x58x64, 3x3x64x64 + ReLU | 10.5 ms (3) | 10.5 ms (3) |
5.68 ms (1)* |

On these workloads the new path is within noise of dispatch-time data
tiling, which already fuses epilogues inside encoded dispatches. *The
global-opt row does not data-tile the convolution, because
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` only affects
dispatch creation. On this machine the existing experimental convolution
data tiling is slower than direct convolution codegen, independent of
this PR.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[Bindings] Fix change HAL bitmask enums to IntEnums instead of IntFlags (#25223)

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Cover the #24932 benchmark matrix in inner_tiled lit tests

Pin the cost model's distribution picks for the #24932 shapes (64^3,
256^3, 81x41x19, 540x516x332) with packed operands from real compiles.
The RVV file sweeps --iree-llvmcpu-number-of-threads=8/4/1 (small shapes
consolidate tiles as threads drop; large stays [18,1,0]; dynamic falls
back to [1,1,0]); the x86 file covers the same matrix at 8 threads.

Assisted-by: Claude Code, Qwen, Doubao

Signed-off-by: Shuangju.Liu <shuangju@multicorewareinc.com>

commit_message:
[Bindings] Fix change HAL bitmask enums to IntEnums instead of IntFlags (#25223)

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.

ci-extra: linux_arm64_clang

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.

ci-extra: linux_arm64_clang

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Build] Use googletest's gtest_main instead of the compiler copy

Rather than renaming the compiler's copy, delete it. It does what
googletest's gtest_main does, so the compiler unit tests now depend on
@com_google_googletest//:gtest_main. Bazel builds that target from
gmock_main.cc, so bazel_to_cmake.py maps it to googletest's gmock_main
CMake target, and both builds link the same main. With only one
iree/testing package left, compiler/src/CMakeLists.txt no longer needs
to add a directory by hand.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Runtime][Python] Preserve DLPack access and ownership

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

Co-authored-by: Tobias Fuchs <9053039+devtbi@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[Runtime][Python] Preserve DLPack access and ownership

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

commit_message:
[Build] Use the compiler gtest_main for compiler unit tests in CMake

In Bazel, the compiler unit tests link
//compiler/src/iree/testing:gtest_main.
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/19237 added that main so that
compiler tests do not depend on the runtime test main. CMake drops the
compiler/src/ and runtime/src/ prefixes from target names, so both
mains map to iree::testing::gtest_main. CMake never added
compiler/src/iree/testing, so the 11 compiler unit tests linked the
runtime main, which parses IREE flags, sets up tracing and links
runtime libraries.

Rename the compiler target to compiler_gtest_main and add its directory
to compiler/src/CMakeLists.txt, so that both builds link the compiler
unit tests against the same main.

Checked with bazel_to_cmake.py (no other changes), bazel query and a
CMake configure without a build: the 11 compiler unit tests link
compiler_gtest_main, and all other test binaries still link the runtime
main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Build] Generate CMake for HALToHALInline and rocm_specific tests

Two test directories had a CMakeLists.txt that bazel_to_cmake.py no
longer generated, so Bazel and CMake ran different tests.

HALToHALInline/test/CMakeLists.txt has been an empty file since
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/14230. bazel_to_cmake.py skips
files without its header and never regenerated it, so the two lit tests
in that directory ran only in Bazel. Regenerate the file.

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/22356 replaced the only test in
tests/e2e/rocm_specific with new suites in tests/e2e/matmul and deleted
the BUILD file, but kept lds_matmul.mlir and the CMakeLists.txt. Since
then, https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/23806 added the RDNA3 WMMA
regression test to the preserved CMake footer, so that test exists only
in CMake. Later, https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/23907 added
im2col_dma_conv.mlir, which no build file references. Restore the BUILD
file and generate the CMake from it:

- The WMMA suite keeps its IREE_ROCM_TEST_TARGET_CHIP gate (gfx11 and
  gfx12). CMake creates the same test as before.
- im2col_dma_conv.mlir becomes a gfx950 suite with the
  requires-gpu-cdna4 label and the flags from its header comment.
  linux_x64_clang runs it under rocjitsu for gfx950, so this is the
  first CI run of this test.
- Delete lds_matmul.mlir. The tests/e2e/matmul suites replaced its
  test, and nothing has run the file since.
- enforce_glob makes Bazel fail to load the package if a new .mlir file
  is not in a suite.

Like all HIP check suites, these suites create no Bazel targets. The
BUILD file declares them, and CMake is generated from it.

Checked with bazel_to_cmake.py (no other changes), bazel query and a
CMake configure without a build: the two lit tests are registered, the
WMMA suite exists for gfx1100 and gfx1201 as before, and the im2col
suite exists only for gfx950.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only

Adds a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to the 28 workflows that
declared no permissions, and drops the top-level `contents: write` and
`pull-requests: write` from clang_tidy.yml (cpp-linter runs with
thread-comments disabled and only needs to read the PR diff).

Jobs that call the GitHub API with the workflow token declare the read
scope they use at job level:
- `pull-requests: read` for the PR diff in clang_tidy.yml and the PR
  description in setup.yml.
- `actions: read` for the cross-workflow artifact download in
  clang_tidy.yml, the run lookup in get_latest_green.sh, and
  `setup_venv.py --fetch-gh-workflow` in the pkgci test workflows.
A called workflow can't exceed its caller's permissions, so the calling
jobs in ci.yml and pkgci.yml grant the same scopes.

Two API failures that used to pass silently now fail the job:
clang_tidy.yml skips clang-tidy only when GitHub rejects the diff as too
large (HTTP 406 `too_large`), and get_latest_green.sh aborts on a failed
`gh api` call instead of counting it as "no green run" and walking the
whole history.

Every write in the release and website workflows still goes through the
`WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT. Checkouts that use the PAT now set
`persist-credentials: false`, so the token no longer sits in
`.git/config` while pip and other dependencies are installed. The two
steps that relied on the persisted credential (the candidate tag push
and `mkdocs gh-deploy`) pass the token explicitly instead.

This takes the OpenSSF Scorecard Token-Permissions check from 0 to 10.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only

Adds a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to the 28 workflows that
declared no permissions, and drops the top-level `contents: write` and
`pull-requests: write` from clang_tidy.yml (cpp-linter runs with
thread-comments disabled and only needs to read the PR diff).

Jobs that call the GitHub API with the workflow token declare the read
scope they use at job level:
- `pull-requests: read` for the PR diff in clang_tidy.yml and the PR
  description in setup.yml.
- `actions: read` for the cross-workflow artifact download in
  clang_tidy.yml, the run lookup in get_latest_green.sh, and
  `setup_venv.py --fetch-gh-workflow` in the pkgci test workflows.
A called workflow can't exceed its caller's permissions, so the calling
jobs in ci.yml and pkgci.yml grant the same scopes.

Two API failures that used to pass silently now fail the job:
clang_tidy.yml skips clang-tidy only when GitHub rejects the diff as too
large (HTTP 406 `too_large`), and get_latest_green.sh aborts on a failed
`gh api` call instead of counting it as "no green run" and walking the
whole history.

Every write in the release and website workflows still goes through the
`WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` PAT. Checkouts that use the PAT now set
`persist-credentials: false`, so the token no longer sits in
`.git/config` while pip and other dependencies are installed. The two
steps that relied on the persisted credential (the candidate tag push
and `mkdocs gh-deploy`) pass the token explicitly instead.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization (#24969)

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing layouts during global optimization makes that phase target
aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding tensor
graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their epilogues and
result unpacks.

Add `--iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling`. For a module with a
single target that supports host encoding materialization
(`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported`: llvm-cpu on x86_64 or AArch64
with the CPU encoding resolver and without inner-tiled layouts), and
with the default encoding strategy, the new pass:

1. normalizes contraction dimensions,
2. assigns and propagates encodings,
3. materializes them on the host,
4. records the target (#24968).

Other modules, and the padding encoding strategy, keep dispatch-time
data tiling. The route takes its operation families and encoding
strategy from the dispatch-creation data-tiling flags, passed down from
`Pipelines.cpp`, because unsupported modules fall back to that route.

**Behavior changes that are easy to miss.**
- The flag takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags,
so conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set.
- The target is recorded even when nothing was data-tiled, so
dispatch-time assignment stays off for that module.
- The early pipeline also runs `BubbleUpExpandShapes` and `SinkReshapes`
on eligible modules.
- For modules with the attribute, dispatch creation always enables
`fuse-mmt4d` and `fuse-data-tiled-convolution` (#24967), even if they
are set to false, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions.

**Relation to existing paths.** `--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` with
early materialization also materializes on the host, but it has no
contraction normalization or propagation, and its mmt4d ops are not
fused with their epilogues. Like that path, this one relies on
`MaterializeHostEncodingPass` and is restricted to single-target
modules. The layout decision is split between this pass,
`isHostEncodingMaterializationSupported` and the dispatch-creation
passes that read the attribute, and it adds HAL and Codegen dependencies
to the global phases. TODOs (#25031) describe moving it into its own
component that decides per affinity.

**Performance** on an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32,
`--iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host`, median of 10). HAL dispatches in
parentheses. x86_64 has not been measured.

| workload | dispatch-time data tiling | this PR |
`--iree-global-opt-data-tiling` |
|---|---|---|---|
| matmul 512x1024x1024 + bias + ReLU | 1.49 ms (4) | 1.50 ms (3) | 1.43
ms (4) |
| batch_matmul 16x256x512x256 + ReLU | 1.69 ms (3) | 1.68 ms (3) | 1.75
ms (4) |
| conv NHWC 1x58x58x64, 3x3x64x64 + ReLU | 10.5 ms (3) | 10.5 ms (3) |
5.68 ms (1)* |

On these workloads the new path is within noise of dispatch-time data
tiling, which already fuses epilogues inside encoded dispatches. *The
global-opt row does not data-tile the convolution, because
`--iree-dispatch-creation-experimental-set-data-tiling-ops` only affects
dispatch creation. On this machine the existing experimental convolution
data tiling is slower than direct convolution codegen, independent of
this PR.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[Runtime][Python] Preserve DLPack access and ownership

Sharing CPU tensors through DLPack must preserve the producer's storage,
access permissions, and lifetime. The fixed import defaults cannot express
host or read-only memory, and unchecked shapes and offsets can expose
invalid memory. Allow callers to specify placement and access, validate
metadata before import, and use the buffer protocol to keep NumPy views
within the mapped range and retain their owner. Make capsule consumption
transfer ownership exactly once, reject exports whose permissions legacy
DLPack cannot represent, and avoid discard mappings when exporting
existing contents.

Co-authored-by: Tobias Fuchs <9053039+devtbi@users.noreply.github.com>
Assisted-by: Codex
Signed-off-by: Christopher McGirr <mcgirr@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Bindings] Fix change HAL bitmask enums to IntEnums instead of IntFlags (#25223)

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.

commit_message:
[Bindings] Fix change HAL bitmask enums to IntEnums instead of IntFlags (#25223)

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 made MemoryType,
BufferCompatibility, BufferUsage and MemoryAccess nanobind IntFlags. On
Python 3.11.0 to 3.11.3, `MemoryType.HOST_LOCAL |
MemoryType.DEVICE_VISIBLE` then fails with "ValueError: 86 is not a
valid MemoryType".

Drop py::is_flag() from the four enums. As IntEnums they keep
`__index__`, which https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25163 added,
and `|` and `&` return plain ints, as
they did before.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Cover the #24932 benchmark matrix in inner_tiled lit tests

Pin the cost model's distribution picks for the #24932 shapes (64^3,
256^3, 81x41x19, 540x516x332) with packed operands from real compiles.
The RVV file sweeps --iree-llvmcpu-number-of-threads=8/4/1 (small shapes
consolidate tiles as threads drop; large stays [18,1,0]; dynamic falls
back to [1,1,0]); the x86 file covers the same matrix at 8 threads.

Assisted-by: Claude Code, Qwen, Doubao

Signed-off-by: Shuangju.Liu <shuangju@multicorewareinc.com>
